source.observed_pattern: A MySQL/MariaDB migration inserts one synthesized configuration row from conditional aggregate expressions and uses HAVING with a NOT EXISTS subquery to suppress the insert when the destination key already exists.
source.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as an independent snapshot initializer: fixed source settings are reduced with MAX(CASE), whitespace is normalized with TRIM and NULLIF, a missing-region guard is evaluated in HAVING, and an existing snapshot row prevents a duplicate insert. Table names, values, labels, and application context are new.

fixture_notes: North has two source settings and is inserted as one normalized snapshot; south already has a snapshot and must not be overwritten; east has no source rows and is not targeted by the fixed north projection.
determinism_notes: All source values, target keys, and aggregate expressions are fixed; the final primary-key read is ordered, with no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent schedules.
setup: CREATE TABLE region_settings (setting_id INT PRIMARY KEY, region_code VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL, setting_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, setting_value VARCHAR(64) NULL)
CREATE TABLE region_snapshots (region_code VARCHAR(16) PRIMARY KEY, snapshot_value VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL, source_count INT NOT NULL)

INSERT INTO region_settings VALUES (1, 'north', 'primary_endpoint', '  https://north.example.test  '), (2, 'north', 'fallback_endpoint', 'https://fallback.example.test'), (3, 'south', 'primary_endpoint', 'https://south.example.test'), (4, 'east', 'primary_endpoint', NULL)

steps.sql: INSERT INTO region_snapshots (region_code, snapshot_value, source_count) SELECT 'north', COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(MAX(CASE WHEN setting_name = 'primary_endpoint' THEN setting_value END)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(MAX(CASE WHEN setting_name = 'fallback_endpoint' THEN setting_value END)), ''), 'unset'), COUNT(*) FROM region_settings WHERE region_code = 'north' HAVING NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM region_snapshots existing WHERE existing.region_code = 'north')

INSERT INTO region_snapshots (region_code, snapshot_value, source_count) SELECT 'south', COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(MAX(CASE WHEN setting_name = 'primary_endpoint' THEN setting_value END)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(MAX(CASE WHEN setting_name = 'fallback_endpoint' THEN setting_value END)), ''), 'unset'), COUNT(*) FROM region_settings WHERE region_code = 'south' HAVING NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM region_snapshots existing WHERE existing.region_code = 'south')

checks.sql: SELECT region_code, snapshot_value, source_count FROM region_snapshots ORDER BY region_code
